inline_comments.comment: `CHANGE_DETECTION_TYPE_ID = 'storybook/change-detection'` duplicates `CHANGE_DETECTION_STATUS_TYPE_ID` already exported from `storybook/internal/types` (see `code/core/src/shared/status-store/index.ts:57`). Defining a second local constant for the same string literal creates two sources of truth that can silently drift. Remove this constant and import `CHANGE_DETECTION_STATUS_TYPE_ID` from `storybook/internal/types`.

The PR moves `'status-value:error'` from index 1 to after `'status-value:warning'` in `statusOrder`. If this array is used as the sort comparator for context-menu status links (e.g., `statusOrder.indexOf(a) - statusOrder.indexOf(b)`), the change inverts the error/warning display ordering — warnings will now appear before errors in the menu. Errors conventionally have higher severity than warnings and should sort first. Verify this is intentional; if the goal is consistency with `statusPriority` in `utils/status.ts` (where higher index = more critical), the sort call should be descending, not ascending.

`getChangeDetectionStatus` is a pure status-data utility with no UI concerns, but it is defined in the React component file `Tree.tsx` and exported from there. All peer utilities (`getMostCriticalStatusValue`, `getGroupStatus`) live in `utils/status.ts`. Placing it here couples the utility to the component module, makes the export boundary surprising, and forces the test file to import from a UI component. Move it to `utils/status.ts` alongside its siblings.

The SVG icons added to `StatusIconMap` for `new`, `modified`, and `affected` are structurally identical to the icons returned for those same statuses by `getStatus()` in `utils/status.ts`. Two separate icon definitions for the same statuses must be kept in sync manually. If `StatusIconMap` is only used within the leaf-node render path, consider replacing its lookups with calls to `getStatus(theme, value).icon` to have a single source of truth.

The two `StatusButton` elements are rendered as separate, adjacent flex children of `LeafNodeStyleWrapper` (which uses `justify-content: space-between`). Without a wrapping container they will be laid out as individual flex items and may be spaced apart from each other rather than grouped as a unit. Wrap them in a `display: flex` container (e.g., `StatusSlots`) so the two slots behave as a single right-aligned group.

`BranchWithChangeDetectionPriority` is first constructed via `makeDualSlotStory(...)`, which sets a `render` function internally, and then that `render` is immediately overridden on the next lines. The render produced by `makeDualSlotStory` is never used. Either accept a `selectedItemId` parameter in `makeDualSlotStory` and pass `dualSlotParentId`, or define this story inline without the helper to make the intent clear and avoid the dead assignment.

The test imports `getChangeDetectionStatus` from `'../components/sidebar/Tree'`, a React component module. Importing a utility function from a component file creates an undesirable coupling and is inconsistent with the existing test file's imports from `'./status'`. This would be resolved naturally by moving `getChangeDetectionStatus` to `utils/status.ts`.

The test case `'branch/group combined priority: error beats new'` directly calls `getMostCriticalStatusValue`, not `getChangeDetectionStatus`. It is not testing dual-slot splitting behavior and is misplaced inside `describe('dual-slot status splitting')`. Move it into the existing `describe('getHighestStatus')` block (or a similarly named block) where the other `getMostCriticalStatusValue` tests live.

The fixture uses keys `first`, `second`, `third` that do not match the `typeId` field values (`'storybook/change-detection'`). `StatusByTypeId` is `Record<StatusTypeId, Status>` — keys are supposed to equal the typeId. The `as unknown as StatusByTypeId` cast silently hides this structural mismatch. A reader who inspects this fixture may incorrectly infer that key and typeId can differ in production. Either align the keys with the typeId values (e.g., use `'first/change-detection'` etc. as distinct typeIds, each mapping to its own Status) or add a comment explaining why the test intentionally uses mismatched keys.

general_comments.comment: None of the five new stories (`WithChangeDetectionOnly`, `WithChangeDetectionAndTestStatus`, `WithTestStatusOnly`, `WithAffectedStatus`, `BranchWithChangeDetectionPriority`) include a `play` function. The project guidelines require story variants to include `play` functions with DOM assertions to validate rendered output and prevent regressions. At minimum, each story should assert that the expected `data-testid="tree-change-status-button"` or `data-testid="tree-status-button"` buttons are (or are not) present in the rendered tree.

The `makeDualSlotStory` helper returns a story with both `args` and a `render` function, but does not include `name` or `parameters.docs.description`. Since the five stories share the same data shape and only differ in their status map contents, adding a one-line comment in each story export (or a `name` field) would help reviewers and Storybook UI users understand the scenario each variant exercises without having to decode the `allStatuses` object.
